idiom_name: pino stream/transport (or winston transport) chaining node:crypto createHmac
implementation_notes: Node ships the crypto (node:crypto createHmac) but not the chokepoint, so a logging library supplies the second half: a pino stream/transport - or a winston transport - receives serialised records and can chain an authenticator before writing. Keep the chain state in exactly one transport instance, write with an append-mode stream or fs.appendFile, and redact at the logger level so the tagged bytes never contain a secret; the hand-written logger is only justified when the audit stream must be structurally independent of the application logger.
pitfalls: Async transports buffer: a chain state that runs ahead of what is durable loses the guarantee on crash, and unbounded buffers turn an audit sink into a memory leak.
JSON.stringify order is insertion order and number formatting is Node's - if the verifier re-serialises from objects instead of re-reading the stored bytes, the chain will not match.
Pino redaction happens on the logger's configured paths, not inside the transport; anything not covered reaches the chained bytes, so define the audit schema and redact before the tag is computed.
